messages:
support-bot: NEW ESCALATION from support: customer 'acme-forms' reports p99 increase on /v1/generate (redwood-v1-small) starting ~2026-03-15T10:02Z. No 5xxs, but p95 600ms -> 1.8s and p99 spikes to ~3s. Request ids: rQ7f, rQ7g, rQ7h. See ticket https://redwood.internal/t/INC-14287

alice: copying repro and raw request the customer sent. they say small prompts (~6 tokens) and bursty traffic after auth refreshes. Customer attached a simple loop repro: 
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-small","input":"Hi"}' &
  done
wait
```
They also included a short trace: a few requests show 401 then immediate retry and a long wait before completion.

sam: looking at traces now. origin of latency seems correlated with continuous-batcher coalesce timing + retries. current cluster config: continuous_batcher.linger_ms=6, min_coalesce_size=2. For tiny prompts that linger is too short, creating a lot of tiny batches and increased scheduling jitter. Also saw arrival jitter when token-refresh retries happened -> bursts that confuse the coalescer.

devon: I pulled host-level traces for the tenant's shard. KV cache hit rate low (they mostly do one-shot prompts), which increases per-token cost but not huge. The tail is dominated by batching behavior: when a burst hits, queue fills then the coalescer holds a tiny fraction waiting for more, but if retries interleave you get lots of subbatches and head-of-queue blocking.

maya: quick mitigation options: 1) bump linger_ms to 20ms for the shared small-prompt pool (should reduce tiny-batch churn), 2) set a force_flush_threshold of 64 tokens, 3) temporarily route acme-forms to the deterministic microbatcher. We can do (1) as a safe canary.

sam: agree. plan: rollout linger_ms=20 to canary pool A (10% nodes) at 10:20Z, monitor p95/p99 and token throughput. If stable, promote to 100% by 10:40Z. Also add a short-lived rate-limit guard on retries to prevent auth-refresh storms from creating arrival jitter.

nate: on the auth side I saw KMS latency spikes around same window causing refresh to fail -> retries. I've raised KMS ticket (KMS-789) and will add client-side jitter/backoff tweaks so we don't hammer endpoints on transient KMS slowdowns. Also recommend limiting retry count to 2 for auth refresh to avoid retry storms.

maya: deploy commands (will run from control-plane):
```text
deploy config "continuous-batcher:linger_ms=20" --target canary-pool-A
monitor metrics: infra.coalesce.batch_count, infra.coalesce.avg_size, infra.latency.p95, infra.latency.p99, tenant=acme-forms
```

infra-bot: deploy started by maya at 2026-03-15T10:20:12Z. canary: pool-A (12 nodes). CI checks passed.

sam: initial canary looks promising: p95 dropped from 1.4s -> 700ms, p99 from ~3s -> ~1.1s on canary hosts. avg batch size jumped from 1.2 -> 3.8. No increase in CPU observed.

alice: customer says they'll accept the temporary change. I'll keep them posted and mark as mitigated for now.

devon: follow-ups: 1) we should add a detector to flag when auth-refresh 5xx/401 rate correlates with batching churn, 2) test client-side retry/backoff docs for customers, 3) long-term consider adaptive linger: increase when average prompt length < X and arrival variance > Y.

nate: KMS team acknowledged transient slow path and will patch keyring hotpath. I created a short runbook note: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-retry-guidance

alice: marking ticket INC-14287 as mitigated, will reopen if p99 regresses after full rollout. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary promotion completed at 2026-03-15T10:35:20Z. global rollout scheduled in 5m; monitoring alert set: if p99 > 1.5s for 5m revert to previous config automatically.
